controller.title: Add a controller with its manifest
controller.about: Install the manifest of a new kind of controller, onboard a controller of that kind and give it its agent.

chapters.text: A controller is added through the agentic MCP. For a kind it does not know yet, first give it the controller's manifest: a YAML file describing its API.
Under A new kind of controller: Upload a manifest. Here, metro.yaml, the example in the agentic MCP's repository (manifests/example).
Installed: Example metro controller is now among the kinds it knows.
Then onboard the controller itself, under Onboard one by its address: a key, a label and its base URL.

Kind: leave it on recognise it from its API: the agentic MCP reads the controller's API and matches it to the manifest just installed. With a password, give the names of the variables that hold the credentials (in controllers.env), never the secrets.
Onboarded, and checked against the common contract: its verdict and any gaps.
Reload CANAH gives it its agent: CANAH can now read it and work it.
Its detail: which parts of the contract it covers, with which of its own operations, and what it lacks.
Done: ask CANAH about it in the chat, like any other controller.

guide.title: Draft a manifest from a user guide
guide.about: When a controller has no manifest: let the agentic MCP draft one from its user guide or API document.

chapters.text: No manifest for a controller? The agentic MCP can draft one from the controller's user guide or API document (text, Markdown, HTML, OpenAPI or PDF).
Under A new kind of controller, name the kind the guide is for…
…then Upload a document: here the example's user guide (manifests/example/metro-user-guide.md).
A manifest for metro2 was drafted: it is among the kinds it knows. A draft states no verb on its own: onboard with this kind, then check its verdict.
Then onboard the controller as in the previous tutorial: the agentic MCP matches it to the drafted manifest.
Done.

contract.title: Change the common contract
contract.about: Load a contract file, check what it changes for every controller, and apply it.

chapters.text: The common contract is the list of verbs (read devices, read links, provision…) every controller is checked against. It is on the SDN controllers page.
On the left, the contract in use: its parts and their verbs, and the file the agentic MCP keeps it in.
To change it, edit it on the right, or load a contract file (JSON).
The file is loaded into the editor. Nothing has changed yet.
Check first: it shows what each controller's verdict would become under this contract, without changing anything.
Each controller's verdict under the new contract, beside the current one: changes are highlighted.
Apply makes it the contract (root only). The agentic MCP keeps the previous one as a backup.
Applied: its version, its parts and verbs, what was added or removed, and where the backup is.
Every controller is checked against the new contract from now on. Done.
